sourceEnglishObjective: Say no, not yet and never, and ask for more or less
candidateObjective: Use Japanese negative expressions and compare quantities while reporting jobsite supplies.
candidateFocus: まだ～ていません means not yet; 誰も～ません and 何も～ません pair an indefinite word with a negative ending. 決して～ません means never. もっと requests more; ～より少ない compares quantities.
curriculumAdaptationNote: Source contrasts never, nobody, nothing, not yet and more/less while reporting supplies. Japanese negative-polarity expressions such as 決して～ません, 誰も～ません and 何も～ません require a complete negative predicate, not standalone scored words. Confirm the countable-material and equipment senses.

cards.reviewNote: Source nada is general 'nothing'; archived 何もありません asserts that nothing exists. The isolated card needs a context-neutral or qualified phrase decision.
Source menos is 'less' and can also apply to countable items in context; archived 少なく is an adverbial form. Choose a contextual headword, especially beside source fewer shingles.
Source otro covers 'another' and 'other'; archived もう一つ is one more item. Keep the isolated face null until its full range is represented or a specific sense is selected.

cards.sourceEnglish: Nobody goes up without a harness.
cards.archivedJapanese: フルハーネスなしで上がる人はいません。
cards.archivedEnglish: Nobody goes up without a full-body harness.
cards.reviewNote: Source says only harness; archived フルハーネス adds full-body specificity. A qualified roofing/source reviewer must decide the equipment term before selecting it.
